annotations.title: Let his hart be changed.
annotations.text: In what maner king Nabuchodonoſor vvas changed is hard to explicate. ◦ But omitting other opinions, the moſt probable and common is, that he vvas not depriued of his reaſonable ſoule, nor the forme and partes of his bodie ſubſtantially changed from the nature of a man: but he was diſtracted loſing the vſe of reaſon, and in his owne melancholie imagination and phantaſie, thought that he was a beaſt. And therfore eaſily refuſed the conuerſation of men, and conſorted himſelf with beaſts; vvent naked; his hayre growing very much, and couering al his bodie; his nayles likewiſe extreme long; he went on his handes together with his feete, like fourfooted beaſtes; did eate graſſe as an oxe, putting his mouth to the ground, to ſhere and ſwalowe it, the ſpace of ſeuen yeares. Then God reſtoring to him the vſe of reaſon, and inſpiring him with grace, he lifted vp his eyes to heauen (v.31.) and in perfect ſenſe bleſſed God, the Higheſt, and prayſed him; was againe receiued, yea ſought for by his nobles and magiſtrates: ſo vvas reſtored to his kingdom, and had more magnificence then before.

notes.text: Nabuchodonosor was not chaged in substance; but became madde, and liued seuen yeares like a beast.

annotations.title: Now therfore I Nabuchodonoſor praiſe, magnifie, and glorifie God.
annotations.text: Albeit holie Scripture doth not reporte, when and hovv king Nabuchodonoſor died, [1] yet by this laſt thing written of him, it is very like he liued not long after his great chaſtiſment: for if he had, it is probable that Daniel would haue written more of him, & that he being ſo fully conuerted to God, vvould haue deliuered Ioachin king of Iuda, out of priſon (which his next ſucceſſor Euilmerodach did. 4. Reg. 25. v. 27.) and al the Iewes from captiuitie, if God had longer ſpared him life, he being now wel affected tovvards them. [2] And that he died in ſtate of ſaluation, may with great reaſon be ſuppoſed, ſeing his repentance and conuerſion to God is ſo fully expreſſed in holie Scripture, and no mention that he fel againe. Which is alſo the iudgement of moſt lerned vvriters, Namely of Ioſephus. li. 10. Antiq. Dorotheus in Synopſi. S. Epiphanius, in vita Danielis. S. Ierom. epiſt. 7. ad Letam. S. Auguſtin epiſt. 122. ad Victoriam, & li. de predeſt & gratia c. 15. Where he compareth Pharao with Nabuchodonoſor, and their diuers endes, by Gods grace mouing the one to penance for his iniquitie, the other wilfully fighting againſt Gods merciful veritie. as we haue noted. Exo. 7. pag. 174.

notes.text: It is probable that he died shortly after his restauration.
And most like that he is eternally saued.
